subject: Re: Model fit follow-up and quantization trade-study
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Mike Lee <mike.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Model fit follow-up and quantization trade-study

Thanks for your time today �14 great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so were all aligned:

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: deploy an on-prem/private instance for Acme's clinical summarization pipelines with strict latency SLAs and auditability.
- Key constraints: high throughput for batch nightly jobs, sub-200ms P50 inference latency for interactive triage UI, and SOC2/audit log requirements.
- Risk area: quantization could materially impact clinical QA scores; you asked for empirical trade-study guidance.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Well run a 200-prompt eval (the attached prompt_set_v1.txt) against the models below and share CSV results.
2) Run AWQ/GPTQ quant variants and include an FP8 candidate where hardware is available  focus on Mistral-7B, Redwood-13B-v1, and Falcon-40B as the primary candidates.
3) Redwood team to provide benchmark CSV, latency/throughput baselines, and a short risk note on quality regression for each quant method.
4) Follow-up 30-min sync next week to review results and agree on pilot config.

Model candidates (shortlist):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (good quality/cost balance; AWQ may yield strong throughput improvements)
- Redwood-13B-v1 (instruction-tuned; should preserve quality under careful quant)
- Falcon-40B (higher quality for complex summarization but heavier; consider GPTQ or mixed FP8 cautiously)

Attachments Ill send in the next message: acme_benchmark_results.csv (baseline runs), prompt_set_v1.txt (200 prompts), and a short trade-study PDF (awq_gptq_tradeoffs.pdf).

Questions for you before we run: any prompts you want prioritized (e.g., long clinical notes vs short triage)? Also confirm whether the on-prem hardware supports FP8 (NVIDIA-Hopper class) or we should exclude FP8 from the first pass.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
---

Thanks Marissa  this looks good. A couple quick clarifications before you run the eval: 

- We definitely want long clinical notes prioritized (examples attached on our side)  can you add 50 long notes and 150 mixed-length prompts to the set?
- Our infra team confirmed we do not have FP8 hardware in our current pilot cluster, so please exclude FP8 for now and note where FP8 would help.
- Most important: can you call out the expected qualitative impact of AWQ vs GPTQ on instruction-following quality? We had a vendor previously where AWQ introduced a small but measurable drop in factuality on summaries (which triggered manual review).

If you can share the baseline CSV and a short summary of the trade-offs by EOD tomorrow thatd be great. Also looping in Mike to make sure procurement timelines remain visible.

Sarah
Sr Product Manager, Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Mike Lee <mike.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T12:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model fit follow-up and quantization trade-study

Appreciate the quick note, Sarah  thanks for confirming FP8 availability. Well exclude FP8 from the pilot and include a separate FP8 note describing where it would have helped (hardware, expected gains).

Ive attached the baseline CSV and the prompt set we discussed (attached as prompt_set_v1.txt). Quick executive summary of the trade-offs (full details in awq_gptq_tradeoffs.pdf attached and the shared Drive link below):

Short summary (pilot-focused):
- AWQ: Best throughput improvements on 7B-class and many 13B variants; generally 2–3x token throughput improvements depending on batch/sequence lengths. Trade-off: instruction-tuned/fine-tuned models can see small regressions on factuality and instruction adherence  typically concentrated on edge-case prompts. We recommend gating AWQ results with a targeted QA set (well run a 2000-sample regression check if you want deeper coverage).
- GPTQ: More conservative quantization approach for larger models (30B+); lower risk of quality regression vs AWQ on instruction-following tasks but less aggressive size/speed gains.
- FP8: High upside for throughput and memory but requires Hopper-class GPUs and a validated runtime path; not part of the initial pilot based on your infra note.

Attached files: acme_benchmark_results.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, awq_gptq_tradeoffs.pdf
Shared files: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_drive_link
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-QLF-17

Proposed pilot config (what well run unless you object):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: FP32 baseline, AWQ quant variant
- Redwood-13B-v1: FP32 baseline, AWQ quant variant
- Falcon-40B: FP32 baseline, GPTQ quant variant

Metrics well capture per-config: ROUGE, BLEU, factuality score (model vs reference), P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, and prompts flagged for hallucination.

Next steps: well kick off the runs today and share the CSV results + an initial short deck by tomorrow EOD. If youre good, Ill schedule a 30-min review for next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model fit follow-up and quantization trade-study

Quick internal notes for the pilot runs and what to watch for:

1) AWQ details
- Use AWQ-4 and AWQ-8 presets where available; AWQ-4 tends to be safer for instruction-tuned checkpoints.
- For Mistral-7B we typically see good stability with AWQ-4; measure token-level perplexity and our factuality probe to detect regressions early.

2) GPTQ guidance
- For Falcon-40B, use per-channel GPTQ and keep a mixed-precision path ready so we can fall back to FP32 for failing prompts.

3) FP8 note (since Acme has no FP8 HW)
- Worth adding a short FP8 appendix for later: expected 2–3x memory reduction on bigger models and an extra ~1.5–2x throughput on Hopper, but requires runtime testing for kernel correctness.

4) Evaluation plan
- Run the 200-prompt pilot, then expand to a 2k-sample QA sweep if AWQ shows any drop >2 points on factuality.
- Tag prompts by "clinical-length" and "edge-case" so we can prioritize manual review where regressions concentrate.

5) Ops/Credentials
- Marissa: please request a short-lived test token for the on-prem sandbox (we’ll need it for automated runs).

I’ll start the batch jobs once we have the test token and Sarah’s 50 long-note samples.

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
